## Current B1 (#302)

`B1.toml` now binds the selected #298 endpoint and the unchanged adopted #255 shared values and R2 law. `prepare.py` materializes its declaration and excludes Kuranov rows 28 and 72. `agent-heavy env PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python analyses/solvent_specification_mdea/run.py` performs fixed replay and comparisons without fitting. [Verification](results/adoption-302/verification.json) gives 278 rows, cost 374.5190788052401, relative cost difference 2.7600e-13 and zero prediction difference. [Pressure assessment](results/adoption-302/B1/pressure-summary.json) gives Xiao 28.1910414167% and Ermatchkov 18.2705616155% AARD.

The [MDEA workflow disposition](../mdea_mea_workflow/notebook.qmd) records the post-hoc owner gate amendment and all limits: two active bounds (+1 protonated-MDEA–bicarbonate interaction and 7 Å Born diameter), conditional parameter uncertainty in #307 below, no F4 evidence at 394.94–395.00 K, the two Kuranov and seven corrected-Kamps domain exclusions, and unavailable 333.15 K / 60 wt% B1 heat. A3 is unchanged and unrefit; it is historical and transfer-penalty evidence. No absorber-use qualification or new physical validation follows.

## B1 errors by temperature, law range and source (#320)

This section aggregates retained rows. It evaluates no model, fits nothing and adopts nothing. [`retained_statistics.py`](retained_statistics.py) reads the stored observed and predicted values and writes [`retained-statistics-320.json`](results/retained-statistics-320.json). It has not been independently reviewed or promoted.

**Definitions.** For pressures, AARD = mean(|predicted − observed| / observed) × 100, the average absolute relative deviation used for Part I's pressures. Bias is the mean of (predicted − observed) / observed × 100, so a negative bias is underprediction. For heat, heat capacity and density the natural measure is the absolute error in the property's unit, so the tables give the mean absolute error and the mean signed error (predicted − observed) with units. Percent values for those properties are shown only for comparison with the pressure rows.

**Law range.** The MDEAH⁺ dissociation law of Kamps & Maurer (b = −819.7, c = 10.976) was measured over 278–368 K ([reaction-basis-kamps-maurer.json](../mdea_mea_workflow/results/reaction-basis-kamps-maurer.json), `source_findings.range_K`; printed p. 1509). B1 declares the law to 395 K, so any B1 state above 368 K uses the law outside its measured range.

The totals reproduce the retained [pressure summary](results/adoption-302/B1/pressure-summary.json) (Ermatchkov 18.2705616 %, Xiao 28.1910414 %). The Ermatchkov aggregate mixes in-range and extrapolated conditions: inside the range B1 underpredicts (bias −11.59 %), and at 393.15 K, outside it, B1 overpredicts (+21.93 %), so the small overall bias (−1.68 %) comes from cancellation. All Xiao rows are inside the range and are underpredicted at every temperature.

Scaled RMS is the retained [replay summary](../mdea_mea_workflow/results/refit-298/B1-endpoint/replay-summary.json) value. Heat values are negative, so a negative signed error means the model heat is more exothermic than the measured heat. The Merkley 388.71 K heat comparison lies above 368 K and is outside the dissociation law's measured range; the model result there is an extrapolation of the law. The 30 Kuranov rows outside the range lie at 373.14–373.17 K and 393.12–393.15 K. The Carson, heat-capacity and loaded-density rows carry no temperature field in the retained rows, so they are not split by law range. The Kim (water–MDEA) and unloaded-density rows contain no CO₂, so the MDEAH⁺ dissociation law does not enter them. The percent bias is given for pressures only: heats are negative, so a percent bias on a heat reverses its sign relative to the signed error.

The current B1 record has 278 fitted rows (67 Kuranov, with Kuranov rows 28 and 72 excluded); the 280-row counts in the historical section below belong to the earlier record.

## Historical specification reproduction

The remainder records earlier wheels and endpoints. `B1-historical.toml` preserves their old B1 binding; the old R2 fit and R4 execution commands below are historical, superseded by the fixed replay above. Their retained outputs are not relabeled as the current record.


The specification-driven calculations reproduce the retained B1 and A3 endpoints and the declared B1 phase-state subset in [issue #228](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/228). These are numerical reproduction checks against the #222 calculations. They establish neither new physical validation nor qualification for absorber use. Delivered evidence awaits independent review and investigator promotion.

The shared [TOML declarations](declarations.toml) own species supports, reactions and their temperature-domain amendment, the neutral reference, seven named problem templates, observation constructors, row column maps, roles, residual scales and weights. Preparation performs fixed source transformations; it defines no chemistry or observation constructor and imports no historical script. The generated per-row problem document was removed.

Delivery-review corrections retain the same numerical scope. The MDEA ideal-gas heat capacity is the retained Neumann-primary cubic, recentered at 313.15 K: $C_p=\sum_k a_k(T-313.15\,\mathrm K)^k$. Native evaluation at the anchor gives 198.77937643331074 J/(mol K). The prior uncentered Wangler label was incorrect; coefficient values are unchanged. The handoff hashes the parameter and caloric preparation provenance.

Coordinate declarations now dispatch `kind = "reaction_coordinate"` and `kind = "reaction_enthalpy_shift"` to the respective native constructors, with `name`, origin, scale and bounds, plus coefficient or pivot temperature. The check follows Engine commit d513820, `engine/docs/equations.md`, `reaction_constant_coordinate_derivative`, and the `Coordinate` and `reg.reaction_coordinate` docstrings: $q=\mathrm{origin}+\mathrm{scale}\,v$ assigns a stored coefficient of natural $\ln K$. For a source enthalpy increment $h$, $\delta a=h/(RT_p)$ and $\delta b=-h/R$, preserving $\ln K$ at $T_p$. The production path uses the Engine constructor, native physical coefficient rows (`EvaluatedCoordinates.physical`, after the EOS and held-diameter rows) and completed native enthalpy-shift laws (`reaction_laws`); the direct formula appears only in the numerical comparison.

On retained Kuranov row `fit:11` at 333.13 K, the objective at zero optimizer value is 0.1264081715573054. Assigning $a=a_0+0.2$ gives cost 0.5571628213373777 versus direct-law cost 0.5571628213373779. A 1000 J/mol shift about 313.15 K gives cost 0.1603266808251767 versus 0.16032668082517665 from the directly modified law. Both zero optimizer values reproduce the unshifted pressure 162212.48927863713 Pa. The largest cost difference is 2.22e-16, below the 1e-10 numerical-equivalence tolerance. [Coefficient evidence](results/reaction_coordinate-check.json) and [enthalpy-shift evidence](results/reaction_enthalpy_shift-check.json) retain both zero and nonzero cases. Fitted reaction declarations from those native chart outputs are now retained in the fit report and consumed by the handoff.

The missing/nonfinite split-coordinate check now precedes exponentiation. A focused failure-injection assertion retains a −∞ trial as one unresolved record with its cause and zero gas-evolution classifications. This assertion tests failure reporting; it is not a physical phase observation. The prior R4 trials contain no such nonfinite coordinate and remain the independently confirmed reproduction evidence.

For [issue #230](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/230), the hand-off now exports eight species with unchanged Engine charges, molar masses and available aliases, explicit element and analytical-component incidence, template-specific supports and analytical feed membership. All eight formula charges equal the Engine charges. All four reactions have exactly zero C, H, N, O and charge imbalance; the three analytical-component rows also close exactly. Three species have ideal-gas caloric records; five ionic species use reaction/reference completion. The neutral reference records the empty override mapping and effective `PureLiquid` solvent / `InfiniteDilution` solute choices. Reaction records state direction, extent units, K basis and reference identities. These are declaration and numerical verification results; absorber qualification remains with the column.

The six property groups in `assessment.properties` retain calibration/outside-fit row regions (temperature, unloaded analytical amine mass percent and CO₂ loading), separately evaluated regions, available-row relative-error statistics, unavailable rows and causes, fitted bounds and links to the existing phase-search evidence. `available_rows` counts all Available records, including zero observations; AARD uses only available nonzero observations. Both Böttinger bicarbonate datasets have 58 available rows and no unavailable rows; each AARD uses 57 nonzero observations. For saturation-capped heats, `region.loading_mol_per_mol` retains requested caps, while `evaluated_region.loading_mol_per_mol` uses only available retained native `endpoint_loading` values, without substituting caps for missing endpoints. The evaluated loading ranges are [0.25808584895232506, 1.009] for calibration-Merkley and [0.15815614361212915, 0.15815614361212915] for outside-fit-Merkley-outside. Zero analytical amine makes CO₂ loading per mole MDEA undefined: both loading regions for calibration-Kim-water are null with the stated zero-MDEA cause; its pressures, temperature and mass-percent ranges and AARD remain unchanged. These row ranges are not continuous validity domains or uncertainty estimates. Derivative actions remain unassessed. The `handoff` command consumes retained endpoint/comparison results; with prediction and fitting calls disabled it produces byte-identical repeated exports, and all 39 listed file hashes match. The existing test file gives four passes, with R1 cost 374.4520134237422 and maximum weighted-residual difference 4.546019116702382e-11. The immutable wheel hash matches the value above. Independent delivery review remains open. The fitted parameter document and its export/reload check remain unavailable on this wheel; no serializer adoption is part of #230.
